entities.summary: Radu Ștefan Mazăre is a Romanian ex-politician. His political activity began with his election to the lower house of the Parliament on the Democratic Party (PD) list, which he left in 1997 to serve as an independent. In 2000, he defeated all party-supported contestants to be elected mayor of Constanța, one of Romania's largest cities and its foremost seaport. Joining the Social Democratic Party (PSD) in 2003, he went on to win the following three elections with a comfortable majority. In 2015, during his fourth term, Mazăre resigned amid accusations of corruption, citing the unbearable stress caused by what he claimed to be politically motivated investigations.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As mayor of Constanța from 2000 to 2014, Radu Ștefan Mazăre implemented various urban development projects, increasing the city's GDP by over 20% during his tenure. His resignation in 2015 amid corruption allegations had a regional impact on Romanian politics.
